proved_step: LEMMA (stage unrolling, closes G0003). Let M be a RAM with S memory cells of w bits. Suppose that for every input x in {0,1}^n, the time between two successive input-bit reads is at most tau (worst case). Then for each interval, the map (configuration at read i, bit x_{i+1}) -> configuration at read i+1 is computed by a Boolean circuit of size tau * poly(S*w), the same for all inputs. Proof: pad each interval to exactly tau steps by idling after halting; unroll the tau steps; each step is a fixed function of the S*w memory bits plus the program counter and register bits, realised with multiplexers for addressing, which costs poly(S*w) per step. The bound is uniform over inputs because tau is a worst-case bound. Scope: this gives the per-interval stage size only. It does not establish Lemma 11's tableau convention (G0001), and it does not establish hypothesis (8).

proved_step: LEMMA (stage size under worst-case vs amortised update time; reduces G0002, does not close it). Setting: M is a RAM with S memory cells of w bits that reads x in {0,1}^N in order; t_i(x) is the number of steps between read i and read i+1 (t_0 before the first read, t_N after the last). (a) If t_i(x) <= u for all i and all x, then the stage map (config at read i, bit x_{i+1}) -> config at read i+1 is computed by a Boolean circuit of size u*poly(S*w), the same circuit for every x, so the N stage circuits give total size Gamma <= N*u*poly(S*w). (b) If only sum_i t_i(x) <= N*u for all x, then every single interval satisfies t_i(x) <= N*u, and (a) with u replaced by N*u gives Gamma <= N^2*u*poly(S*w). PROOF. (a) Pad each interval to exactly u steps by idling after halting; the padding length does not depend on x. Unroll the u steps; each step is a fixed function of the S*w memory bits plus program counter and register bits, realised with multiplexers for addressing at cost poly(S*w). Each stage therefore has size u*poly(S*w), and N stages give N*u*poly(S*w). (b) Each t_j(x) >= 0, so t_i(x) <= sum_j t_j(x) <= N*u for every i and x; apply (a) with u := N*u. SCOPE. Dependency lemma: Lemma 12 (Gamma <= 2^m*poly(s), N = 2^m) follows from (a) and needs a per-interval worst-case bound; the amortised reading only gives 2^(2m) via (b). It does not establish that MMW Thm 1.2 has the per-interval reading (G0002 stays open until the formal definition is quoted from the primary text), does not touch Lemma 11's tableau scope (G0001), and does not touch hypothesis (8). Status: standard RAM unrolling, probably bookkeeping for the desk's purposes.

proved_step: LEMMA (corrected Lemma 11, scope fixed; attacks G0001). Let M be a deterministic single-tape or RAM-style machine with S work cells over a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed state set Q (both constants). Let one update consist of at most tau steps of M, reading one input symbol z in {0,1} at the start. Then the update map (configuration, z) -> configuration is computed by a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit with O(tau*S) gates, where the configuration is encoded as S cells of constant width plus a one-hot head indicator (S bits) plus the state (constant bits) plus, if the input head is kept, its position in log N bits. PROOF: (1) Encode the head position by one-hot indicators h_1..h_S. (2) One step: read symbol r = OR_j (h_j AND c_j), O(S) gates. (3) New cell value c'_j = (h_j AND w(state,r)) OR (NOT h_j AND c_j) where w is a constant-size table over (state,r), O(S) gates. (4) Head shift: h'_j = (h_{j-1} AND move_right) OR (h_{j+1} AND move_left) OR (h_j AND stay), O(S) gates. (5) State update: constant-size table, O(1) gates. Each step costs O(S) gates. Concatenating tau steps gives O(tau*S). Padding to exactly tau steps by idling after halting makes the circuit the same for every z. SCOPE: this proves the bound for a constant-alphabet, constant-state TM with a one-hot head encoding. The input head position needs log N bits of state; if S < log N the input position is not stored and the one-pass claim is not covered. Only O(tau*S) per update is claimed; the RAM variant of the manuscript (poly(S,m) per operation) is not touched. It does not close G0002 (worst-case update time) or hypothesis (8). Reviewer must be of another model family.

proved_step: LEMMA (RAM one-step circuit with explicit polynomial; attacks sub-obligation (i) of G0001, does not close it). Fix a RAM M with a fixed program of P instructions, R registers and S memory cells, all words of w bits, with the instruction set fixed (constant). Its configuration is a bit vector of length B = (S+R)*w + ceil(log2 P) (memory, registers, program counter). Let delta: {0,1}^B x {0,1} -> {0,1}^B be the step function, where the extra bit is the input bit read when the current instruction is an input read. Then delta is computed by a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit of size at most K*P*((S+R)*w + w^2) for an absolute constant K, uniformly in the input bit. PROOF: for each instruction i, (a) indirect addressing: decoding an address word against S cells costs O(S*w) gates by w-bit equality tests and a multiplexer over the S*w memory bits; (b) an arithmetic or move operation on w-bit words costs O(w^2) gates (schoolbook addition, multiplication, comparison); (c) the next-configuration bits for instruction i are a fixed combination of (a) and (b) costing O(B) gates; (d) selecting the instruction by the program counter is a multiplexer over P instruction results, costing O(P*B) gates. Summing over the P instructions gives K*P*(S*w + R*w + w^2 + B) <= K'*P*((S+R)*w + w^2). Padding a time interval to exactly tau steps by idling after halting makes the tau-fold composition a single circuit of size tau*K'*P*((S+R)*w + w^2), the same for every input string. With w <= poly(S,m) (the word width the manuscript uses), this gives poly(S,m) per RAM step, with an explicit polynomial. SCOPE: a fixed finite instruction set and fixed program; word-RAM with w-bit words; no unbounded integers. It does not establish the input-parameter encoding in Lemma 11 (still undefined), does not discharge G0001 as a whole, does not touch G0002 (update-time definition) or hypothesis (8). Not reviewed: claimant is claude-haiku-5-5. Reviewer must be of another model family.

proved_step:
statement: REPAIR of S0021 (Lemma 11 scope). Let N = 2^n. Let M be a machine with S >= n work cells over a constant alphabet and constant state set Q, plus an input-position register p in {0,1}^n counting input bits consumed. One update consumes one input bit z in {0,1} and performs at most tau steps of M. Then the update map (configuration, z) -> configuration is computed by a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit with O(tau*S) gates, the same circuit for every z after padding. Configuration = S cells + one-hot head (S bits) + state + p (n bits).
derivation: (1) Use the one-hot head and cell-update circuit of S0021 steps (2)-(5): O(S) gates per machine step. (2) Increment p with a ripple-carry incrementer: n half-adders, O(1) fan-in-2 gates each, so O(n) = O(S) gates per update. (3) Concatenate tau steps: O(tau*S) gates. (4) Pad to exactly tau steps by idling after halting, so the circuit is independent of z and of the run length. z enters as a wire to the first step; p is not used to address the input, so no N-way multiplexer is needed. (5) Any machine with S < n can be padded to S' = n cells; the bound then becomes O(tau*max(S,n)), which is polynomial in the space bound and does not change the poly(s) accounting.

evidence: Reviewer family: claude-haiku (same as claimant), NON-BINDING. First false line: 'pad each interval ... with dummy queries ... Each oracle query string is a function of the configuration and is fed to a fixed oracle gate'. A fixed-width oracle gate of input length ell receives a real query of length < ell only after padding, and Sigma3SAT^A is a language of exact strings, not padding-invariant, so the answer on the padded string need not equal the answer on the query actually made. Dummy queries are harmless (answers unused); real short queries are not covered. lemma: Proof: for slot j, the configuration fixes the query register q_j (length field plus L bit positions). Indicators I_{j,lambda} = [len(q_j)=lambda] are ordinary logic. Gate O_{j,lambda} receives the first lambda bits of q_j, so when I_{j,lambda}=1 it is evaluated on the exact string q_j. Slot output = OR_lambda (I_{j,lambda} AND O_{j,lambda}), O(L) gates. Unselected gates get a constant input and are masked. Idle or unused slots select a dummy length whose output is masked to 0. Wiring positions are fixed, so the circuit does not depend on x. Scope: stage map only; does not close G0001, G0002, or hypothesis (8). Claimant family claude-haiku-5-5; the reviewer must be from another model family.

evidence: The lemma is mathematically correct for standard RAM-to-circuit conversion: (a) With per-interval worst-case bound u, padding to exactly u steps by idling (copying config to config) and unrolling gives a circuit of size u * poly(S*w) per stage, total N*u*poly(S*w). (b) Amortized bound sum t_i <= N*u implies each t_i <= N*u, giving N^2*u*poly(S*w). The gap is not in the lemma but in its application: the step explicitly notes it does NOT establish that MMW Thm 1.2 has the per-interval worst-case reading (G0002 stays open until the formal definition is quoted from the primary MMW text). As a general RAM-circuit lemma, it survives review.

Reviewed the circuit construction argument: (a) indirect addressing via w-bit equality tests and multiplexer over S cells costs O(S*w) gates; (b) w-bit arithmetic (add/mul/compare) costs O(w^2) gates with schoolbook algorithms; (c) next-configuration combination costs O(B) gates; (d) instruction selection via P-way multiplexer over B-bit results costs O(P*B) gates. Summing over P instructions gives O(P*((S+R)*w + w^2 + log P)) which is bounded by K*P*((S+R)*w + w^2) for absolute constant K since log P <= (S+R)*w + w^2 for non-trivial RAMs. The circuit is uniform in the input bit (input bit is a wire). No argument gap found; this is a standard RAM-to-circuit simulation with explicit polynomial bound. The scope is correctly stated: fixed instruction set, word-RAM, does not establish Lemma 11's input-parameter encoding or hypothesis (8).

Reviewed the circuit construction. Configuration = S cells (constant alphabet => O(S) bits) + one-hot head (S bits) + state (O(1)) + p (n bits). Since S >= n, total configuration bits O(S). One machine step: read cell under head (multiplexer with S inputs, log S selector bits from one-hot head => O(S) gates), write new symbol (O(1) per cell, but only head cell changes => O(S) gates via demultiplexer), update state (O(1)), move head (shift one-hot by 1 => O(S) gates). Total O(S) gates per step. Ripple-carry incrementer for p: n half-adders, each O(1) fan-in-2 gates, total O(n) = O(S) gates. Concatenate tau steps: O(tau*S) gates. Padding to exactly tau steps makes circuit independent of z and run length. z enters as wire to first step. No N-way multiplexer needed since input is consumed sequentially. The construction is correct for the stated model. Scope: this gives the update circuit size bound; it does not by itself establish the full Lemma 11 tableau accounting or hypothesis (8).

Construction verified: for each of tau*q call slots and each lambda=0..L, provision an oracle gate O_{j,lambda} of input length exactly lambda. The circuit computes the query string q and its length l from the configuration (and previous oracle answers), then routes q to O_{j,l} via l-keyed multiplexers. The A-oracle evaluates gates in topological order, so adaptive queries are correctly handled. Query strings are never padded; the circuit is fixed independent of x. This resolves the padding-invariance flaw of S0017.

proved_step: statement: LEMMA (input-position-aware stage circuit). Let M be a deterministic single-tape machine with S work cells over a fixed finite alphabet and fixed state set, processing an N-bit input in order. Suppose each inter-input update uses at most tau machine steps. Encode the work-tape head one-hot, the finite control with a constant number of bits, and the input-head position with b=ceil(log2(N+1)) bits. Then each update map (configuration,z)->configuration has a fan-in-two Boolean circuit of O(tau(S+b)) gates, uniform over configurations and incoming bits z. In particular, its size is O(tau*S) when S>=b. Proof: A single machine step can read the work-tape symbol by OR-ing the S one-hot-selected cell symbols, at O(S) gates; update each cell and the one-hot work head in O(S) gates; and update the finite control in O(1) gates. The input-head position is incremented or held according to the transition, which costs O(b) fan-in-two gates using a ripple-carry incrementer and control gates. Thus one step costs O(S+b). Compose at most tau copies of this step circuit; if the update halts early, make the halted configuration an absorbing state and pad the composition to tau copies. This yields O(tau(S+b)) gates and gives one circuit for every incoming bit and admissible configuration. Since b<=S in the stated special case, O(tau(S+b))=O(tau*S).

statement: LEMMA (length-charged oracle stage simulation). Let M be a deterministic streaming machine with a B-bit configuration. In one input interval it performs at most tau ordinary steps and at most q oracle queries, each of length at most ell. Suppose the fixed oracle language O has a deterministic decider taking at most p(r) steps on every r-bit query, where p is a fixed nondecreasing polynomial. Then the interval transition from (configuration, next input bit) to the next configuration has a uniform fan-in-two Boolean circuit of size O(tau*poly(B) + q*(p(ell)+ell)*log(2+p(ell)+ell)). Proof: Unroll the at-most-tau ordinary machine steps, using an absorbing halted configuration for padding. Each step, including RAM addressing and query generation, has poly(B) gates. For each of the at-most-q query slots, use its generated length r and query bits as input to a circuit simulating the fixed decider on the exact r-bit query. Unrolling a deterministic T-step computation on at most ell input bits gives a fan-in-two circuit of O((T+ell) log(2+T+ell)) gates; select the appropriate exact-length computation using r. Since r<=ell and p is nondecreasing, this costs O((p(ell)+ell) log(2+p(ell)+ell)) per query. Feed each answer into the subsequent machine transition and compose the circuits. This uses no padding-invariance assumption about O. If P=NP and O is in PH, then O is in P, so a fixed polynomial-time decider exists; when B, tau, q, and ell are polynomially bounded in s, the resulting stage circuit is polynomial in s.

evidence: Padding a real query shorter than ell may change its input and answer. No padding invariance is stated for Sigma3SAT^A. Dummy queries do not fix real queries.

proved_step: LEMMA (buffer-explicit exact-query simulation). Let a deterministic streaming machine have a B-bit configuration that includes an ell-bit query buffer and a binary length field. Suppose an interval uses at most tau ordinary steps and at most q oracle calls, each of length at most ell. If its fixed oracle O has a deterministic decider running in at most p(r) steps on r-bit inputs, for a fixed nondecreasing polynomial p, then the interval transition has a uniform fan-in-two circuit of size O(tau*poly(B)+q*(p(ell)+ell)*log(2+p(ell)+ell)). Proof: Encode each query by its length and bits in the included buffer. The decider reads exactly the indicated prefix, so no padding invariance is assumed. Unroll its deterministic computation on at most ell input bits for at most p(ell) steps; the standard tableau-to-circuit construction uses O((p(ell)+ell)log(2+p(ell)+ell)) gates. Wire its answer into the machine transition and compose the at most q query simulations with the at most tau ordinary transitions, each costing poly(B). The resulting circuit is uniform for all configurations and next input bits. This is conditional on the query buffer being included in B and does not establish the manuscript transfer.

evidence: The claim that the update map (configuration,z)→configuration can be computed by a fan‑in‑two circuit of size O(tau·S) is false; the OR of the S one‑hot work‑tape symbols requires fan‑in‑S, so the correct bound is O(tau·S·log S).
The OR of the S one-hot work-tape symbols requires fan-in-S, so any fan-in-two circuit must have size Ω(tau·S·log S), contradicting the claimed O(tau·S) bound.

The update map (configuration,z)→configuration can be computed by a fan‑in‑two circuit of size O(τ·S·log S): a binary‑tree OR selects the one‑hot work‑tape cell (O(log S) gates), cell updates need O(S) gates, control updates O(1); composing τ steps yields O(τ·S·log S) total size, satisfying the fan‑in‑two requirement.

The proof claims a circuit of size O(tau*poly(B) + q*(p(ell)+ell)*log(2+p(ell)+ell)) by 'select[ing] the appropriate exact-length computation using r' for each oracle query of length r <= ell. However, this selection step requires a multiplexer over up to ell different query lengths, which incurs an additional factor of Omega(ell) or Omega(log ell) in the circuit size. The claimed bound O((p(ell)+ell) log(p(ell)+ell)) per query assumes a fixed input length ell, but the machine must handle variable-length queries r <= ell without padding invariance of the oracle decider. Without padding invariance, simulating a decider that behaves differently on inputs of different lengths requires either (a) padding to ell (which assumes padding invariance) or (b) a multiplexer over r=1..ell, adding a factor of ell or log ell. The proof sketch does not justify how to avoid this factor while maintaining fan-in-two and the stated size bound.

Verified that the proof's circuit construction yields O(tau·poly(B)+q·(p(ell)+ell)·log(2+p(ell)+ell)) gates; no extra multiplexer needed because the query buffer provides exact length, so the bound holds.

Corrected lemma: per-interval transition map is computed by a uniform Boolean circuit of size O(tau·poly(S·w)), uniform over all inputs. Proof: pad interval to exactly τ steps, unroll each step using multiplexer-based circuits of O(poly(S·w)) gates; transition function depends only on configuration and input bit, so circuit is uniform. This establishes the size bound without falsely claiming closure of G0003.
